newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
-- Electronic online link-up between the finance ministry's services, corporate entities and their auditors will commence in 1998, starting with monthly statements of value added tax.

-- According to provisional data, Monday's public offering of five- and 10-year inflation-protected bonds with a 4.0 percent coupon only raised some 40 billion drachmas. The finance ministry plans two or three more issues of T-bills and bonds in August to raise around 400-450 billion drachmas against September's high fiscal needs, estimated in excess of 2.0 trillion drachmas.

-- An Athens Court has ruled that a number of terms included in contracts offered by mobile telephony operator Telestet are excessive, thereby necessitating compensation of the company's subscribers. It is expected that the court decision will also impact Telestet's competitor Panafon which offers similar contarcts.
-- The finance ministry hopes to run complete checks by October 1997 on all companies suspected of tax evasion, making use of its new Escort integrated system for cross-reference of tax data.

-- The course of fiscal revenues in September and October will be the key determinants in meeting the national economy ministry's 15.6 percent target for fiscal revenue growth in 1997. The national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou holds frequent discussions with officials from the revenue services of his ministry in search of ways to speed up the collection of taxes in arrears.

-- Mergers in the National Bank group of companies are moving ahead very swiftly. Astir Insurance and National Insurance will hold general meetings on August 19 to receive shareholder approval for the terms of their merger. The procedures for the merger between National Mortgage Bank and National Housing Bank are also at a final stage and are expected to be concluded by year-end.

-- A report by the Economist Intelligence Unit paints a bleak picture for the prospects of Greece's participation in the Economic Monetary Union (EMU). The report says that despite the progress made towards meeting the Maastricht criteria Greece will not be in a position to join EMU on its target date, 2001.
-- Total financial compensation for extended damages in cotton crops by hailstone in the Larissa prefecture of central Greece will exceed three billion drachmas.
-- The official secondary bond market which will be supervised by the Bank of Greece is expected to start operations on January 1, 1997. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
